Add a New Rule Pack

Source: vignettes/add-rule-pack.Rmd
add-rule-pack.Rmd

Why create a custom rule pack?

aRtifacts ships with a core catalog and module builders, but most teams also need project- or organization-specific checks. A rule pack is just a function that returns a list of CoreRule objects.

This vignette shows a practical pattern you can copy:

  1. Write a pack constructor.
  2. Run it on an artifact snapshot.
  3. Track introduced/resolved/persisting flags across cuts.

Step 1 — Start from a target domain 

library(aRtifacts)

lb <- example_sdtm_lb()
head(lb)
#>   STUDYID DOMAIN     USUBJID LBSEQ LBTESTCD     LBTEST LBORRES LBORRESU
#> 1 STUDY01     LB STUDY01-001     1      HGB Hemoglobin    13.0     g/dL
#> 2 STUDY01     LB STUDY01-001     2      HGB Hemoglobin    13.4     g/dL
#> 3 STUDY01     LB STUDY01-002     1      HGB Hemoglobin    -1.0     g/dL
#> 4 STUDY01     LB STUDY01-002     2      HGB Hemoglobin    14.1     g/dL
#> 5 STUDY01     LB STUDY01-003     1      HGB Hemoglobin    15.0     g/dL
#>   LBSTRESN      LBDTC VISITNUM SITEID
#> 1     13.0 2024-01-01        1 SITE01
#> 2     13.4 2024-01-29        2 SITE01
#> 3     -1.0 2024-01-03        1 SITE01
#> 4     14.1 2024-01-31        2 SITE01
#> 5     15.0 2024-01-04        1 SITE02

We’ll target LB-like data keyed by STUDYID, USUBJID, LBSEQ.

Step 2 — Define a custom pack constructor

A pack constructor should:

  • accept configuration (domain, thresholds, ownership),
  • create one or more new_rule(...) objects,
  • return a plain list of those rules.
make_rule_pack_lab_custom <- function(domain = "LB",
                                      owner_team = "Data Management",
                                      hgb_min = 6,
                                      hgb_max = 22) {
  list(

    # Rule 1: Hemoglobin plausibility window
    new_rule(
      id = "LAB001_HGB_OUT_OF_RANGE",
      title = "Hemoglobin out of range",
      topology = "A1",
      scope = "record",
      intent = "clinical_review",
      domain = domain,
      severity = "warning",
      owner_team = owner_team,
      fn = function(data, context, rule) {
        needed <- c("USUBJID", "LBTESTCD", "LBSTRESN")
        if (!all(needed %in% names(data))) return(data.frame())

        testcd <- as.character(data$LBTESTCD)
        value <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(data$LBSTRESN))
        bad <- testcd == "HGB" & !is.na(value) & (value < hgb_min | value > hgb_max)
        if (!any(bad)) return(data.frame())

        data[bad, c("USUBJID", "LBTESTCD", "LBSTRESN"), drop = FALSE]
      }
    ),

    # Rule 2: Result unit should be present when result is present
    new_rule(
      id = "LAB002_RESULT_WITHOUT_UNIT",
      title = "Result present without unit",
      topology = "A1",
      scope = "record",
      intent = "data_entry",
      domain = domain,
      severity = "error",
      owner_team = owner_team,
      fn = function(data, context, rule) {
        needed <- c("USUBJID", "LBTESTCD", "LBORRES", "LBORRESU")
        if (!all(needed %in% names(data))) return(data.frame())

        result_present <- !is.na(data$LBORRES) & nzchar(as.character(data$LBORRES))
        unit_missing <- is.na(data$LBORRESU) | !nzchar(as.character(data$LBORRESU))
        bad <- result_present & unit_missing
        if (!any(bad)) return(data.frame())

        data[bad, c("USUBJID", "LBTESTCD", "LBORRES", "LBORRESU"), drop = FALSE]
      }
    ),

    # Rule 3: Duplicate test on same date for same subject
    new_rule(
      id = "LAB003_DUP_SUBJECT_TEST_DATE",
      title = "Duplicate subject/test/date",
      topology = "A1",
      scope = "record",
      intent = "ops_anomaly",
      domain = domain,
      severity = "warning",
      owner_team = owner_team,
      fn = function(data, context, rule) {
        needed <- c("USUBJID", "LBTESTCD", "LBDTC")
        if (!all(needed %in% names(data))) return(data.frame())

        keys <- data[, needed, drop = FALSE]
        dup <- duplicated(keys) | duplicated(keys, fromLast = TRUE)
        if (!any(dup)) return(data.frame())

        data[dup, needed, drop = FALSE]
      }
    )
  )
}

Step 3 — Run custom pack on an artifact snapshot 

snap <- new_domain_snapshot(
  name = "LB",
  data = lb,
  key_vars = c("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "LBSEQ")
)

art <- new_artifact_snapshot(
  domains = list(LB = snap),
  build_id = "cut-001"
)

custom_rules <- make_rule_pack_lab_custom(domain = "LB")

ctx_v1 <- new_rule_context(current = art)
flags_v1 <- run_rules(ctx_v1, custom_rules)
flags_v1
#>       USUBJID LBTESTCD LBSTRESN                 RULE_ID              RULE_TITLE
#> 3 STUDY01-002      HGB       -1 LAB001_HGB_OUT_OF_RANGE Hemoglobin out of range
#>   TOPOLOGY  SCOPE          INTENT SEVERITY      OWNER_TEAM
#> 3       A1 record clinical_review  warning Data Management

The output contains your flagged rows plus standardized metadata:

  • RULE_ID
  • DOMAIN
  • SEVERITY
  • INTENT
  • OWNER_TEAM

Step 4 — Compare flags between cuts

Now simulate a new cut with one resolved issue and one newly introduced issue.

lb_v2 <- lb

# Resolve an existing issue from sample data (negative LBSTRESN)
lb_v2$LBSTRESN[lb_v2$USUBJID == "STUDY01-002" & lb_v2$LBSEQ == 1] <- 13.8

# Introduce a new issue: missing unit
lb_v2$LBORRESU[lb_v2$USUBJID == "STUDY01-003" & lb_v2$LBSEQ == 1] <- ""

snap_v2 <- new_domain_snapshot(
  name = "LB",
  data = lb_v2,
  key_vars = c("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "LBSEQ")
)

art_v2 <- new_artifact_snapshot(
  domains = list(LB = snap_v2),
  build_id = "cut-002"
)

ctx_v2 <- new_rule_context(current = art_v2)
flags_v2 <- run_rules(ctx_v2, custom_rules)

flag_changes <- compare_flag_states(
  old_flags = flags_v1,
  new_flags = flags_v2,
  by = c("USUBJID", "DOMAIN", "RULE_ID")
)

flag_changes
#>       USUBJID DOMAIN                    RULE_ID     status
#> 1 STUDY01-002   <NA>    LAB001_HGB_OUT_OF_RANGE   resolved
#> 2 STUDY01-003   <NA> LAB002_RESULT_WITHOUT_UNIT introduced

This gives you longitudinal observability:

  • introduced: new findings,
  • resolved: findings that disappeared,
  • persisting: findings still present.

Step 5 — Productionize your pack

For real projects, move your pack constructor into package code:

  • place constructor in an R/ file (for example, R/rule_packs_lab.R),
  • add tests under tests/testthat/ (one test file per pack/module),
  • document expected input columns and output behavior,
  • version your rule IDs and avoid reusing old IDs with new semantics.

A useful pattern is to keep IDs stable and add new IDs instead of changing what an existing ID means.

—dev

Step 6 — Showcase bundle composition

You can combine built-in Core50 packs with your custom pack in one run.

core_rules <- c(
  pack_core_50_schema(domain = "LB"),
  pack_core_50_a1(
    domain = "LB",
    key_vars = c("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "LBSEQ"),
    date_var = "LBDTC",
    numeric_var = "LBSTRESN",
    numeric_min = 0,
    numeric_max = 1000
  ),
  pack_core_50_a2(
    domain = "LB",
    key_vars = c("STUDYID", "USUBJID", "LBSEQ"),
    site_var = "SITEID",
    subject_var = "USUBJID"
  )
)

all_rules <- c(core_rules, make_rule_pack_lab_custom(domain = "LB"))
flags <- run_rules(new_rule_context(current = art_v2), all_rules)

This gives one consolidated findings table while keeping stable rule IDs and ownership metadata across bundles.

What’s next?

  • Use pack_core_50_a1() + your custom pack together: all_rules <- c(pack_core_50_a1(...), make_rule_pack_lab_custom(...))
  • Split large custom packs into smaller module builders (similar to pack_core_50_a1(), pack_core_50_a2(), etc.).
  • If your checks depend on a standard/metadata file, pass it as an explicit argument to the pack constructor.
